_notes: The questions Rome answers one way or another (E1 §4.1), each ordered from its traditional to its progressive end. A document of the record sets an axis on its date; a generated pope moves an axis one step toward his own reading. The bishop's reading (norm) sets his diocese's stance where a system reads it (`stances`: the older Mass first), never above what the law allows (`floor`). Readings and changes are authored; leans and floors are invented and flagged.

axes.label: the older form of the Mass

values.label: said freely
values.gist: restoring to every priest the freedom to say the 1962 Missal
values.change: Any priest who can say the 1962 Missal may say it, and a pastor may give a stable group its Sunday Mass without asking the bishop.

values.label: by the bishop's indult
values.gist: letting the bishops allow the 1962 Missal by indult
values.change: The 1962 Missal may be said only by the bishop's leave, for the groups who ask him for it.

values.label: by the bishop's faculties
values.gist: placing the 1962 Missal under the diocesan bishop, by faculties granted priest by priest
values.change: A priest needs the bishop's faculties to say the 1962 Missal, and no new groups are to be founded in parish churches.

values.label: not said
values.gist: closing the use of the 1962 Missal in the parishes
values.change: The 1962 Missal is not to be said in the parishes; the reformed Missal is the Mass of the Roman Rite.

faculties.enthusiastic: {bishop} wrote within the week. The parish Masses in the older form are to end by Pentecost; he will grant no faculties; the one chapel he allows is named, and it is not a parish church.
faculties.faithful: {bishop} wrote to the clergy: priests who already say the older Mass are to write for faculties by the end of the month, and he will decide each case. No new groups are to be founded.
faculties.minimal: {bishop} wrote that priests who already say the older Mass may go on while their requests are processed, which his secretary lets it be known will take some time.
faculties.slow: {bishop} wrote that {doc} requires study and that, until it has had it, whatever stands in the diocese stands. Several priests read the letter twice to be sure of it.

free.enthusiastic: {bishop} wrote that any stable group who asks is to be given the older Mass, and said it himself at the cathedral before the year was out.
free.faithful: {bishop} wrote that pastors are to receive requests from stable groups generously, as {doc} asks, and to tell the chancery what they have done.
free.minimal: {bishop} wrote that pastors must weigh the unity of their parishes, and that the chancery is to hear of any request before anything is granted.
free.slow: {bishop} wrote nothing for a season, and then that pastors should consult the chancery before acting on any request. The forms, when they came, were long.

values.label: close to the Latin
values.gist: giving the English-speaking Church a translation of the Missal close to the Latin
values.change: The people answer "And with your spirit," the Creed begins "I believe," and every priest learns the Missal again.

values.label: in plain English
values.gist: returning the English Missal to plain speech
values.change: The Missal goes back into plain English: "And also with you," shorter prayers, and new cards in the pews.

axes.label: communion for the divorced and remarried

values.label: refrained from
values.gist: reaffirming that the divorced and civilly remarried refrain from communion
values.change: The divorced and civilly remarried are to refrain from communion unless the first marriage is found null or they live as brother and sister.

values.label: a path of discernment
values.gist: opening a path of discernment for the divorced and civilly remarried
values.change: A divorced and remarried Catholic may walk a path of discernment with a priest, case by case, and some will come to communion by it.

axes.label: blessings of couples in irregular situations

values.label: not given
values.gist: declaring that the Church does not bless couples in irregular situations
values.change: No priest is to bless a couple in an irregular situation, as a couple, in any form.

values.label: brief and spontaneous
values.gist: allowing brief, spontaneous blessings of couples in irregular situations, never in a rite
values.change: A priest may give a brief, spontaneous blessing to a couple in an irregular situation who ask, never in a rite and never with a wedding's trappings.

values.label: the ordinary process
values.gist: on the ordinary process for marriage cases
values.change: A nullity case goes through the tribunal and a second, confirming sentence, and takes a year or more.

values.label: a briefer process
values.gist: reforming the process for declaring the nullity of marriage
values.change: No second sentence is needed, the tribunals are to charge little or nothing, and a clear case may go to the bishop himself in a briefer process.

axes.label: the instituted ministries of lector and acolyte

values.label: for men
values.gist: reserving the instituted ministries of lector and acolyte to men
values.change: Only men are instituted lectors and acolytes; women read and serve at the altar by the pastor's leave.

values.label: open to women
values.gist: opening the instituted ministries of lector and acolyte to women
values.change: Women may be instituted lectors and acolytes by the bishop, in a rite, for good.

values.label: the councils as they were
values.gist: on the proper place of the councils in the government of the Church
values.change: The parish council advises and the pastor decides; nothing is sent to Rome.

values.label: listening sessions
values.gist: asking every parish to be consulted and its voice sent up to Rome
values.change: Every parish is to hold listening sessions, and what it says goes to the diocese, the bishops' conference, and Rome.

values.label: a quiet matter
values.change: Nothing is asked of the parishes.

values.label: a teaching
values.gist: on the care of our common home
values.change: The parishes are asked to preach on the care of creation and to look at their own buildings, lights, and waste.
